$comment: Source of truth for the fingerprint generator's post-generation
self-check and for the generated mutation tests. C++ compiles against
additions/camoucfg/invariants.h, which SP6a will generate from this file;
until then the two are kept in step by hand and
Entries are added by the sub-project that owns the keys they constrain.
An SP is not complete until its invariants are here with a passing
mutation test -- an entry without one is documentation, not enforcement,
and reads as coverage while providing none.

invariants.repair: set ua:platform to the canonical UA-CH platform for the OS family of ua:osInfo
why: ua:osInfo lands in the user-agent string. ua:platform lands in
navigator.userAgentData.platform and in the Sec-CH-UA-Platform request
header. A page reads both without effort, and a Windows user agent
beside a Linux platform is a stronger signal than either value would
be if it were simply honest.
ua:osInfo wins because it is the more visible of the two, so repairing
the other changes less of what pages actually see.
A key that is absent, or present but unrecognised, constrains nothing.
This entry catches values that CONTRADICT one another; an absent key
constrains nothing for this relational entry because the incoherence
an absent partner creates -- one channel spoofed, the other silently
reporting the real OS -- is reported by the startup diagnostic in
content/browser/browser_main_loop.cc, not here. An unrecognised value
is a per-key type question rather than a relational one.
SP1a ships this incoherence today and names SP5a as its owner -- see
the comment above ConfigPresentsUserAgentIdentity in
patches/sp1a-ua-producer.patch.
The available screen area is the display minus the OS chrome
(taskbar, dock, menu bar), so it is physically a subset of the
display: screen.availWidth <= screen.width on every real machine,
with equality in the no-taskbar / fullscreen-kiosk case. A
configuration reporting availWidth > width describes a work area
larger than the screen containing it -- a state no real device
produces, and a contradiction a detector reads by comparing two
screen properties.
screen.width is authoritative: it is the display the work area is
carved out of, so the work area is what gives when they disagree.
Both keys are read as GetUint32, the getter sp4a-screen consumes
them with; a value that is absent, or present with the wrong type
(GetUint32 wants a non-negative integer), constrains nothing.
Absent-key posture matches ua-os-family-agrees: this entry catches a
contradiction between two configured values. A lone spoofed key
(availWidth set, width real) is one channel spoofed with the other
reporting the truth, which is the startup diagnostic's to report, not
a relational entry's -- with one value configured there is no
disagreement to demonstrate. An out-of-range single value is SP5b's
to reject.
The height axis of screen-avail-width-fits: screen.availHeight <=
screen.height for the same physical reason, and the same absent-key,
wrong-type and authoritative-key posture applies. Split per axis
rather than folded into one entry because Relation is a binary
comparison over two keys, and the two axes are independent
contradictions -- a config can violate one without the other.

invariants.repair: set navigator.platform to the canonical reduced platform for the OS family of ua:osInfo
why: ua:osInfo lands in the user-agent string; navigator.platform is its
own JS property. A page reads both, and a Windows user agent beside
navigator.platform === 'MacIntel' is a textbook OS tell. The reduced
User-Agent freezes one canonical platform per OS -- Win32, MacIntel,
Linux x86_64, Linux armv81 -- so the correct value is a function of
the claimed OS, and any other explicit value contradicts it.
A canonical-STRING compare, not a same-OS-family one: Linux and
ChromeOS both report 'Linux x86_64' under UA reduction, so they share
one platform bucket. A family-level check would wrongly flag a ChromeOS
claim beside 'Linux x86_64' as a mismatch.
ua:osInfo is authoritative, so navigator.platform is the value the log
names as wrong. This is the EXPLICIT-value complement of the SP1b
navigator.platform derive, which fills the key from the claimed OS only
when it is ABSENT (an explicit value wins over the derive). The two are
disjoint: the derive fires on an absent key, this entry on a present
one. Same absent-key and unrecognised-value posture as
ua-os-family-agrees; a ua:platform-only OS claim (no ua:osInfo) is out
of this entry's reach, and the startup diagnostic warns on it instead.
Deferred to SP5a by the derive's measurement doc
(2026-09-07-navigator-platform-derive.md) as kSamePlatformBucket.
